signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Repricing
signals.text: NZD/JPY displays the widest G10 divergence this week, anchored by JPY 1W average gains of +1.433% across 7 pairs against NZD 1W losses of -0.941% across 4 pairs, creating an active 2.374% leader-to-laggard spread. The structural carry spread favors NZD via a +175bp policy differential with RBNZ at 2.75% against BoJ at 1.0%, yet aggressive BoJ rate-hike repricing completely overrides the yield gap. Institutional consensus now places a 97% probability on a BoJ hike to 1.25% at the September 18 meeting, bolstered by comments from US Treasury officials reducing political hurdles for tighter Japanese policy. Meanwhile, NZD speculative positioning sits heavily short at leveraged funds net -23,004 contracts, residing in the 4th percentile of its 52-week range with z at -1.81. The pair trades below its technical benchmarks, with NZD/USD holding below its SMA20 at 0.5907, SMA50 at 0.5850, and SMA200 at 0.5857. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; policy convergence and aggressive JPY momentum dominate nominal carry. Catalyst: BoJ interest rate decision 18 Sep — hike to 1.25% priced at 97%. Risk: BoJ holds rates unchanged at 1.0%, triggering an immediate unwinding of aggressive JPY longs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Policy Repricing
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.57, positioned below its SMA20 at 158.16, SMA50 at 159.98, and SMA200 at 158.42. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal prints at an extreme -2.31 put skew, showing heavy institutional demand for downside protection against USD weakness. Leveraged funds hold an extreme net short JPY position of -111,297 contracts (2nd percentile, z -2.18), expanding by -29,678 contracts on the week, which clashes directly with the options market's protective positioning and the 97% economist consensus pricing a BoJ rate hike to 1.25%. While Fed at 3.75% versus BoJ at 1.0% maintains a +275bp policy rate advantage for the dollar (and +266bp via SOFR-TONA carry), VRP trades negative at -0.6% (IV 10.8% versus HV30 11.3%), reflecting market complacency relative to realized volatility. With VIX at 16.5 representing normal volatility, the downside pressure reflects direct monetary policy repricing rather than broader safe-haven demand. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; crowded speculative shorts face severe squeeze risk into tightening Japanese policy. Catalyst: US CPI release 10 Sep at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US Core CPI prints above the 0.2% monthly forecast, reigniting broad dollar yield demand.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7224, holding above its SMA20 at 0.7159, SMA50 at 0.7060, and SMA200 at 0.6998. CFTC data shows institutional leveraged funds heavily net long AUD at +50,250 contracts, situated in the 94th percentile of its 52-week range (z +1.79), even as net exposure trimmed by -3,328 contracts WoW. In stark contrast, retail sentiment registers an extreme 91% short positioning, setting up an active institutional versus retail divergence at historical extremes. The currency pair is underpinned by the Reserve Bank of Australia at 4.35% versus the Federal Reserve at 3.75%, delivering a 60bp carry advantage to AUD (+71bp via AONIA-SOFR). Implied volatility sits at 7.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.9%, reflecting a modest 1.2% vol risk premium that supports carry stability under normal volatility conditions with VIX at 16.5. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; institutional long positioning and positive carry maintain upward trend structure against trapped retail shorts. Catalyst: US CPI release 10 Sep at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds accelerate weekly net long liquidation, triggering broader profit-taking toward the SMA20 at 0.7159.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% — 60bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Policy Decision + Real Rate Compression
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1637, positioned above its SMA20 at 1.1625 and SMA50 at 1.1525, while remaining capped just below its SMA200 at 1.1638. The Federal Reserve at 3.75% holds a 135bp nominal policy rate spread over the European Central Bank at 2.4% (+145bp via SOFR-ESTR basis), yet the real policy rate differential sits narrower at 129bp (USD real rate +1.35% versus EUR +0.06%). Options markets indicate balanced near-term sentiment with 25-delta risk reversals near neutral at -0.11 and 1M ATM implied volatility at 5.0% against HV30 of 4.2%, yielding a modest 0.8% volatility premium. Leveraged funds hold net short exposure of -52,784 contracts, though net positioning has rebuilt by +20,265 contracts over the trailing 4 weeks to the 31st percentile. The impending ECB refinancing rate decision presents direct policy event risk ahead of US inflation figures. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; nominal dollar carry advantage balanced by tightening real yield spreads and moving average resistance. Catalyst: ECB Main Refinancing Rate decision 10 Sep at 12:15 UTC. Risk: ECB delivers an unexpected 25bp rate hike, forcing immediate short-covering through the SMA200 barrier at 1.1638.
